heading: RBI FD Rule Changes: Impact on Your Interest Rates
tldr: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed banks to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits.
This differentiation can be based on a bank's liquidity risk under the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework.
The primary goal is to provide banks with more flexibility in managing their liquidity requirements efficiently.
While the rule directly impacts bulk deposits (₹2 crores and above), it could indirectly influence retail FD rates over time.
Savers should regularly compare fixed deposit offerings from various banks to ensure optimal returns.
caption:
Big news for your savings! The RBI just made a change that could affect how much interest your bank pays you on fixed deposits. Banks now have more freedom to set different rates, especially for larger deposits. Over time, this might even change rates for smaller FDs. It's a good reminder to always check different banks for the best returns. Read more to understand what this means for your money.
